TMEM

Package Install

Install TMEM Package from GitHub

Install the package from github

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("eriklarsen4/TMEM")

Install TMEM Package from CRAN

Alternatively, if the package is accepted by Bioconductor, install from Bioconductor

# Install from Bioconductor
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("TMEM")

Attach TMEM Package

library(TMEM)

We’ll use the datasets included in the TMEM package to demonstrate its functions.

Functions

get_GO_info

  • A crucial function of the TMEM package is the get_GO_info function that gathers ALL the gene ontology information of a list of gene or protein identifiers

  • This is called gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA)

  • The GSEA conducted on this dataset is included in full in a markdown of another repository, along with additional analyses for that paper

  • There, we used the statistical results directly from the geneontology.org website; this pre-dated the clusterProfiler package

  • The get_GO_info function gathers all the relevant information in one place without needing to generate multiple files and analyses across 1+ browsers– it’s all in-house

  • However, there are (unsurprisingly) discrepancies between geneontology.org’s annotations and Bioconductor’s

  • Furthermore, Bioconductor does not employ geneontology.org’s gene ontology nesting structure (see the vignette), which effects statistics (also not provided by Bioconductor) a user might try to extract

  • While the clusterProfiler package effectively does gather this, it is limited to only significantly enriched terms which can be abritrary at times, especially for small datasets

  • For now, I recommend using the get_GO_info function for exploratory work and plotting, while relying on geneontology.org’s web browser directly, or the clusterProfiler package for publication statistics

  • The statistical discrepancies are noted in the examples section of this markdown

## First import the data in the package
data("aDRG_DEG_list")

## pass the variable into the function (data was derived from mouse)
results <- TMEM::get_GO_info(list_of_interest = aDRG_DEG_list[c(1:30)],
                             species = 'mouse')
  • Inspect results by unpacking everything from the returned list
  ## GO INFO about each Unique GO returned by the list
GO_info_by_term_df <- results |> 
  purrr::keep_at("GO_info_by_term_df") |> 
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(., ~gsub(.x, pattern = 'GO_info_by_term_df\\.', replacement = ''))

  ## GO INFO about each gene in the list
gene_GO_info_df <- results |> 
  purrr::keep_at("gene_GO_info_df") |>
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(., ~gsub(.x, pattern = 'gene_GO_info_df\\.', replacement = ''))

  ## every alias for each gene in the list
aliases <- results |> 
  purrr::keep_at("aliases")

  ## all aliases from the list without the genes of the list
list_of_interest_aliases <- results |> 
  purrr::keep_at("list_of_interest_aliases") |>
  unlist() |> 
  as.character()

  ## Unique GOs returned by the list
unique_GOs <- results |> 
  purrr::keep_at("unique_GOs")

  ## Unique GO IDs returned by the list
unique_GO_IDs <- results |> 
  purrr::keep_at("unique_GO_IDs")
  • Print the GO_info_by_term_df to the console
head(GO_info_by_term_df)

                                               list_of_interest = aDRG_DEG_list[c(1:30)])

Print the ortholog_and_alias_fn output to console

head(ortholog_df)
## # A tibble: 6 × 7
##   ref_species target_species input_gene ortholog_gene input_ensg         ortholog_ensg      description                                                  
##   <chr>       <chr>          <chr>      <chr>         <chr>              <chr>              <chr>                                                        
## 1 mouse       human          Il31ra     IL31RA        ENSMUSG00000050377 ENSG00000164509    interleukin 31 receptor A [Source:HGNC Symbol;Acc:HGNC:18969]
## 2 mouse       <NA>           Il31ra     <NA>          ENSMUSG00000050377 <NA>               <NA>                                                         
## 3 mouse       macaque        Il31ra     IL31RA        ENSMUSG00000050377 ENSMMUG00000017394 interleukin 31 receptor A [Source:VGNC Symbol;Acc:VGNC:73624]
## 4 mouse       human          Shtn1      SHTN1         ENSMUSG00000041362 ENSG00000187164    shootin 1 [Source:HGNC Symbol;Acc:HGNC:29319]                
## 5 mouse       fly            Shtn1      Frl           ENSMUSG00000041362 FBgn0267795        Formin-like                                                  
## 6 mouse       macaque        Shtn1      SHTN1         ENSMUSG00000041362 ENSMMUG00000007578 shootin 1 [Source:VGNC Symbol;Acc:VGNC:77333]
  • I recommend passing the list of genes with their aliases, (c(list_of_interest_aliases, aDRG_DEG_list)) to the get_GO_info function

query_GO

Background

Want to find multiple genes/proteins annotated to certain GO Terms?

This can be useful for: + investigating molecular pathways + investigating complexes (for cross-checking or discovery) + finding multiple GO Terms that contain a regular expression string

Example

query_GO_results <- TMEM::query_GO(model_org = 'human',
                                   string_terms = 'dense core vesicle|lysosome')

  • Extracting the gene/protein IDs associated with the GO Terms derived from the given regular expression(s) is non-trivial, depending on the function call.

  • Those gene/protein IDs associated with a given term can be extracted directly using dplyr without storing all the function’s results to an object in the global environment:

query_GO_results |> 
  purrr::keep_at("GO_df") |> 
  as.data.frame() %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(., ~gsub(.x, pattern = 'GO_df.', replacement = '')) %>%
  dplyr::rename_with(., ~gsub(.x, pattern = '\\.\\.', replacement = 'N.')) |>
  dplyr::filter(GO.Term == 'endolysosome membrane') |> 
  dplyr::select(Genes) |> 
  dplyr::pull() %>%
  stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |> 
  head()
## [1] "CTSB" "CTSK" "CTSL" "CTSS" "LGMN"

find_row_Z

Background

  • This function computes a Z-score for a provided matrix, currently agnostic to grouping

  • This is highly useful for generating heatmaps

Example

aDRG_TPM <- TMEM::aDRG_TPM
TMEM::find_row_Z(Expression_Profile = aDRG_TPM[c(1:5),]) |> head()
##           GeneID  WT1  WT2  WT3  WT4 Mut1 Mut2 Mut3 Mut4
## 1      -343C11.2  Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf  Inf  Inf -Inf
## 2 00R_AC107638.2 -Inf  Inf  Inf -Inf -Inf  Inf -Inf -Inf
## 3      00R_Pgap2 -Inf -Inf  Inf -Inf  Inf  Inf -Inf -Inf
## 4  0610009O20Rik  Inf -Inf -Inf -Inf  Inf  Inf -Inf  Inf
## 5          1-Mar -Inf  Inf -Inf -Inf  Inf  Inf -Inf -Inf

Example Uses

Finding Genes Related by a Generic GO Term relevant to a list of interest

  • Interested in finding genes/proteins related to a certain cellular phenomenon?

  • When there are multiple terms involving a certain GO phrase (i.e.  organelles or processes), search GO terms with regular expressions!

  • Obviously, this provides larger scope than investigating a specific term

GO_info_by_term_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(grepl(GO_Term, pattern = 'dense core vesicle')) |> 
  dplyr::select(Gene_IDs_from_List) |> 
  dplyr::pull() %>%
  paste0(., collapse = ';') %>%
  stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |> 
  unique() |> 
  head()
## [1] "Sst"

  • Similarly, the results returned by the get_GO_info function include all the information on all the GO Terms– not just including the genes/proteins from the list of interest that are associated with a GO Term (these IDs are called “Overlap”)

  • It provides all the IDs associated with the GO Term

  • clusterProfiler does not– it only includes statistically enriched terms

GO_info_by_term_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(grepl(GO_Term, pattern = 'dense core vesicle')) |> 
  dplyr::select(Gene_IDs) |> 
  dplyr::pull() %>%
  paste0(., collapse = ';') %>%
  stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |> 
  unique() |> 
  head()
## [1] "Adcyap1" "Adrb1"   "Adrb2"   "App"     "Avp"     "Bdnf"
  • Lastly, to find those IDs across generic GO Terms NOT also in the provided list of IDs:
"%notin%" <- Negate("%in%")

c(GO_info_by_term_df |> 
    dplyr::filter(grepl(GO_Term, pattern = 'dense core vesicle')) |> 
    dplyr::select(Gene_IDs) |>
    dplyr::pull() %>%
    paste0(., collapse = ';') %>%
    stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |> 
    unique() # All the genes in all the GO Terms
  )[
    which(
  c(GO_info_by_term_df |> 
      dplyr::filter(grepl(GO_Term, pattern = 'dense core vesicle')) |> 
      dplyr::select(Gene_IDs) |>
      dplyr::pull() %>%
      paste0(., collapse = ';') %>%
      stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |> 
      unique()
  ) %notin%
  c(aDRG_DEG_list ) == TRUE
)
] # All the genes in all the GO Terms indexed by those that are NOT in the list 
##  [1] "Adcyap1"  "Adrb1"    "Adrb2"    "App"      "Avp"      "Bdnf"     "Cacna2d1" "Calca"    "Cck"      "Chga"     "Crh"      "Dvl1"     "Fzd8"     "Gnai2"    "Hcrt"     "Htr1d"   
## [17] "Igf1"     "Kif1a"    "Npy1r"    "Oprd1"    "Oxt"      "Pdyn"     "Penk"     "Plat"     "Plcb2"    "Ptprn"    "Tac1"     "Cadps"    "Calcrl"   "Npff"     "Ghrl"     "Stxbp5"  
## [33] "Npy"      "Stxbp5l"  "Slc18a2"  "Grp"      "P2rx2"    "Dmxl2"    "Vps13a"
    # of interest

Finding Genes Related by Multiple Precise GO Terms

  • Interested in which genes from your list of interest overlap across multiple GO Terms?
c(GO_info_by_term_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(GO_Term == 'neuronal dense core vesicle' |
                  GO_Term == 'regulation of cell migration') |> 
  dplyr::select(Gene_IDs_from_List) |> 
  dplyr::pull() %>%
  paste0(., collapse = ';')%>%
  stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';'))[which(GO_info_by_term_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(GO_Term == 'neuronal dense core vesicle' |
                  GO_Term == 'regulation of cell migration'
                ) |> 
  dplyr::select(Gene_IDs_from_List) |> 
  dplyr::pull() %>%
  paste0(., collapse = ';') %>%
  stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |> 
  duplicated() == TRUE
)]
## [1] "Sst"

Finding GO of Any Number of Genes

  • When a user is interested in all of the Go Terms that are shared by multiple gene/protein IDs from the user’s list of gene/protein IDs:
gene_GO_info_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(GeneID == 'Lpar3' |
                  GeneID == 'Lpar5') |>
  dplyr::select(GO_Terms) |> 
  dplyr::pull() %>%
  paste0(., collapse = ';') %>%
  stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |>
  unique() |> 
  head()
## [1] "MAPK cascade"                              "cell morphogenesis"                        "regulation of cell growth"                 "G-protein alpha-subunit binding"          
## [5] "molecular_function"                        "transmembrane signaling receptor activity"
  • Similarly, repeating the above for just one gene/protein is simpler– remove the | in the dplyr::filter command and subsequent GeneIDs:
gene_GO_info_df |>
  dplyr::filter(GeneID == 'Il31ra') |> 
  dplyr::select(GO_Terms) |> 
  dplyr::pull() %>%
  stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |> 
  head()
## [1] "regulation of protein phosphorylation"             "positive regulation of protein phosphorylation"    "columnar/cuboidal epithelial cell differentiation"
## [4] "glandular epithelial cell differentiation"         "immune system process"                             "inflammatory response to antigenic stimulus"

Finding Genes of a Specific GO Term

GO_info_by_term_df |> 
  dplyr::filter(GO_Term == 'neuronal dense core vesicle') |> 
  dplyr::select(Gene_IDs) |> 
  dplyr::pull() %>%
  paste0(., collapse = ';') %>%
  stringr::str_split_1(., pattern = ';') |> 
  head()
## [1] "Adcyap1" "Adrb1"   "Adrb2"   "App"     "Avp"     "Bdnf"
